key_insight: Automatically generated derivatives enable differentiable high-order mesh r-adaptivity with accurate optimization gradients, Hessians, and mesh sensitivities.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports mesh optimization and consistent sensitivity analysis for inverse engineering problems while reducing manual derivative development.
method: Define local mesh-quality objectives using the Target-Matrix Optimization Paradigm.
Use ∂FEM to generate pointwise first-, second-, and mixed-order derivatives.
Apply finite element operator decomposition for CPU/GPU execution, matrix-free Hessians, and implicit mesh sensitivities.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments report GPU solve times comparable to hand-derived TMOP on a benchmark, improved adaptation convergence, and material-interface identification in an inverse heat-conduction problem.
watch_item: Consistent implicit mesh sensitivities depend on sufficiently converged stationarity equations and a well-conditioned mesh Hessian.
